rv.q: This razor-sharp production has crisp, clear direction.
It’s a modern, compelling and extremely relevant production.

This might easily be dismissed as a stage stunt had Burns not produced an interpretation of the work that turns one of the so-called ‘problem plays’ into a terrific piece of contemporary theatre that grips from start to finish.
Emily Burns’ lucid modern-day adaptation paints a bleak picture of a corrupt political system

Director Burns tries to carve a polemic out of Shakespeare’s raw material but is ultimately confounded by the bizarre motives and contemporary misogyny of the play, which leave Isabella stranded in a modern interpretation that offers her nowhere to go.
The crucial ambiguity inherent in the silence duly preserved, if a little over-egged, this Measure is properly powerful...

Measure for Measure has been described as one of his 'problem plays' but in this very fine edited version, it resonates wonderfully in today's society with the counter position of moral dilemmas, political expediency, human base instincts and the corruption of power.
In Emily Burns’ remarkable production the contemporary link cannot be missed.

cn.t: Emily Burns' modern adaptation of Shakespeare's problem play earns praise for its timely resonance with contemporary power dynamics and hypocrisy. Critics laud the streamlined, intense production as gripping and superbly performed.
